date_enacted: 2026-06-16 (Carroll County Quorum Court unanimous adoption of Emergency Ordinance 2026-17)
trigger: Immediate pause on high-impact industrial and high-intensity digital infrastructure facilities (reported by contemporary coverage to include data centers, artificial intelligence computing facilities, and cryptocurrency mining facilities) in unincorporated Carroll County while the county develops a permitting and public-notice framework
current_status: Active as of 2026-09-23. The 12-month emergency moratorium (Ordinance 2026-17), unanimously adopted by the Quorum Court on 2026-06-16 and effective immediately, remains in force with no reported repeal, extension, or replacement; its 365-day term runs through 2027-06-16. Corroborated by a second independent local news source (the Eureka Springs Independent's contemporaneous meeting report) beyond the original KY3 broadcast story, and by three specialty policy trackers (ServerCountry, SAVRN, AI GridWatch) that separately cite the ordinance number and June 16 vote. A complete signed county copy of the ordinance was still not located on the county's website or in Municode as of 2026-09-23, so the underlying record remains multiple independent news accounts rather than a primary ordinance document. date_enacted: The Town Board of the Town of South Fork introduced and passed Emergency Ordinance No. 2026-03 on June 18, 2026, per the archived legal notice published in the Valley Courier's July 1, 2026 edition. The notice's own adoption clause misstates the enacting body as 'Town of Center,' which is judged to be a drafting/scrivener error: every other part of the notice -- its heading ('TOWN OF SOUTH FORK'), all WHEREAS recitals, and the operative sections (which reference amending 'the South Fork Revised Municipal Code' and 'the South Fork Zoning Code') -- identifies the Town of South Fork, and the neighboring Town of Center's own published board-meeting calendar shows no meeting on June 18, 2026 at all.
duration: One-year pause on permit and site-development applications for new primary-use data centers while the town considers code amendments and community engagement.
legal_basis: Town of South Fork Emergency Ordinance No. 2026-03. The ordinance's own adoption clause names 'Town of Center' rather than South Fork, but this is judged a scrivener's error (see date_enacted): the heading, every recital, and every operative section name South Fork, and the Town of Center's own agenda calendar (via towncloud.io) shows no board meeting on June 18, 2026.
current_status: Active as of 2026-09-23; jurisdiction confirmed as the Town of South Fork (see legal_basis). Per Section 4 of the ordinance, the one-year pause on data center site-development and permit applications expires the earlier of June 18, 2027, or the effective date of South Fork Revised Municipal Code/Zoning Code amendments addressing data centers, whichever occurs later (the ordinance's own internal 'earlier of ... whichever occurs later' drafting, quoted verbatim). No repeal or amendment found.

trigger: City Comprehensive Plan and Land Development Code do not address data centers; SB 484 (Ch. 2026-65) authorizes local regulation; SB 180 storm-recovery freeze in effect through Oct 2027 for Volusia County
current_status: Active as of 2026-09-23; 18-month citywide moratorium on all data center types, adopted 5-0 on second reading 2026-08-25 (first reading 2026-07-28), while staff draft Comprehensive Plan and Land Development Code amendments intended to ban large-scale data centers.
